<h1 align="center">Castaway</h1>

<p align="center">
  <b>Ten hours of lo-fi island, scored like a capture-the-flag contest with one player, who is mostly idling.</b><br>
  <sub>Unofficial. Inspired by the small-island routines of the 1992 screensaver <i>Johnny Castaway</i>, and not affiliated with it or its owners.</sub>
</p>

**Castaway** (working title) is a stationary-frame lo-fi video for YouTube, in the spirit of the 10-hour lofi streams: a young woman alone on a tiny island with one tall palm, a raft and a lot of time. She mostly idles, nodding to the music in her headphones. Every so often, something happens. Then she goes back to nodding. Sunny, hand-painted, 16:9 at 1080p, and always daytime.

The board above keeps score the only way a contest with one player can. Every gag is a challenge, filed under the timer that brings it round, and the rarer it is, the more it is worth: a coconut sip scores 100, walking off over the sea and coming back with an iced coffee scores 1000. The teams are the schedule's lanes, which play at the same time, so the sea can score while she is busy with a coconut. Every activity starts on the next bar of the music, so the solves land on the beat. And for most of the contest the scoreboard is frozen, because she is idling. That is the contest. Every sound in it is synthesized from code.

```sh
python tools/serve.py     # then open http://127.0.0.1:8765/
```

<details>
<summary><b>Rules</b>: categories, points, the freeze and the tie-break</summary>
<br>

[`activities.toml`](activities.toml) lists more than 90 activities, each with its own timer tier, and other sessions keep adding more. The run counts below are the median of 200 simulated 10-hour runs, as the file's own header puts them. The points are this board's invention.

| Category | Comes round | In a typical run | On the board |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Regular | every 2 to 5 minutes | about 155 | 100 |
| Occasional | every 12 to 25 minutes | about 30 | 250 |
| Rare | every 30 to 60 minutes | about 13 | 500 |
| Super rare | every 3 to 6 hours, at most 3 a run | about 2 | 1000 |
| Chained | when another gag starts it | about 20 | 50 |

**Teams.** One per lane: `castaway` (her), `sea_sky` (ships, drones, the shark), `cat`, `turtle`, `shore` (the tide) and `garden` (the kumara). Lanes run side by side, so a ship can sail past while she is busy, and the ship has been known to wait for exactly that. A solve goes to the first lane its activity lists.

**The freeze.** She is busy about a third of the time and idling the rest. On this board the freeze is not the tense last hour. It is the default.

**Ties** go to whoever got there first. In the banner the cat ties `sea_sky` on 500 and loses on time; the kumara ties the tide on 50 and loses on time, being a plant.

**Fairness.** The default run is 10:00:00 with seed 1992. Same seed, same video, event for event, so nobody can claim the island was rigged. It was, but consistently.

</details>

<details>

  Turtle Visit          isle{both_dozed_off}
  Plant a Kumara        isle{it_grows_over_the_video}

RARE  ·  every 30 to 60 min  ·  500 pts
  Delivery Drone        isle{the_parcel_is_more_headphones}
  Signal Hunt           isle{one_bar_at_the_top_of_the_palm}
  Stray Cat             isle{came_by_crate_napped_up_the_palm}
  Shark Nod             isle{same_beat_different_species}

SUPER RARE  ·  every 3 to 6 h, at most 3 a run  ·  1000 pts
  Leave Any Time        isle{back_with_an_iced_coffee}
  Wave for Rescue       isle{it_tooted_back_and_sailed_on}      0 solves

CHAINED  ·  started by another gag  ·  50 pts
  Tide Takes It         isle{the_sandcastle_is_withdrawn}
  Kumara Flowers        isle{pale_lavender_nobody_remarks}

NOT ON THIS BOARD, STILL IN THE SCHEDULE
  a tour boat of selfie-takers (nobody offers a lift), a bro on an electric
  hydrofoil (one shaka, then gone), fire by friction (a flame, then a wave),
  a hammock (no second tree: tied to the raft), a lookout up the palm (the
  palm bends to ground level), spear fishing (a heroic lunge, a miss), and
  a reply to the bottle, hours later, in a different bottle.

<details>
<summary><b>Audio</b>: 0 solves</summary>
<br>

Every sound is synthesized from code by [`tools/make_audio.py`](tools/make_audio.py): no samples, no loops, no recordings, so no third-party licence applies. More than 150 sound files so far. The theme is a seamless 60-second loop at 80 BPM in F major (a ii-V-I-vi progression): 20 bars of exactly 3 seconds, with electric piano, a kalimba lead, soft drums and vinyl crackle. One loop of the banner is one pass of the theme. The ocean is a seamless 60-second loop too. The mix sits at -14 LUFS with true peak at or below -1 dBTP, and levels can be set in the master and per routine.

Nobody has listened to any of it yet. Hence the solve count.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Infrastructure</b>: the renderer and the tools</summary>
<br>

The renderer is a web page ([`web/index.html`](web/index.html), served by [`tools/serve.py`](tools/serve.py)) with a live preview and export to a YouTube-ready MP4. Plain ES modules, no build step, no npm packages. It exports frame-exact H.264 in the browser with WebCodecs (68 to 78 frames a second at 1080p30 in Chrome), and the server mixes the sound and joins the two into an MP4. Hard cuts and stepped movement are the motion defaults.

```sh
python tools/serve.py             # preview + export, http://127.0.0.1:8765/
python tools/schedule.py          # validate the schedule, simulate 10 hours
python tools/render_demo.py --dev # every activity in a row, with a dev HUD
```

[`tools/render_demo.py`](tools/render_demo.py) is the older Python reference renderer. Decisions, rules and open questions live in [`MUSING.md`](MUSING.md).

**Status.** In development. No video has been published, so there is no link, no prize and no closing ceremony. There will, eventually, be a video.

</details>

<sub>The look borrows the generic jeopardy board and scoreboard that capture-the-flag contests have used for years; no platform's name, logo or theme is copied, and the teams are the schedule's own lanes, not people. Castaway is unofficial and the owner's own work. The 1992 screensaver that inspired it belongs to its owners.</sub>
